SUBJECT:  AMENDINGTHECITY'SZONINGCODEBYMODIFYINGTITLEII,CHAPTERII,21
OF  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  TO  RELAX  OR  REMOVE  RESTRICTIONS  ON  THE
SIZE  OF  WAREHOUSES  AUTHORIZED  IN  THE  CITY'S  URBAN  MIXED  USE  ZONES  AND
COMMERCIAL  INDUSTRIAL  ZONES

PURPOSE:  To consider  two  alternate  resolutions  regarding  proposed  changes  to Chapter  11.21  of the South
Gate Zoning  Code (which  is set forth  in Title  11 of the South  Gate  Municipal  Code).  The first  resolution,  if
approved  by the Plaru'iing  Comtnission  ("Conu'nission"),  would  be to recoirunend  to the City  Council  ("Council')
that the City's  Zoning  Code  be revised  to eliminate  size limitations  on warehouses  in the City's'  Urban  Mixed
Use Zones  and Commercial  Industrial  Zones.  The second  resolution,  if approved  by the Commission,  would
direct  the City's  Corni'nunity  Development  Department  staff ("Staff')  to study the matter  further  and return  to the
Commission  at a later date with  recommendations.  The resolutions  are intended  to be alternative  approaches  to
the issue and have been written  with  the intention  that the Commission  can approve  either  resolution  but should
not approve  both.  The Commission  also has the option  of not approving  either  of the two  resolutions,  which
would  effectively  signify  the Corninission's  desire that the Zoning  Code not be amended.

At the request  of the Applicant,  this  item  was continued  from  the Planning  Commission  meeting  on March  5,
2024.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Staff recommends  that the Commission  take the following  actions:

  a.  CONDUCT  a public  hearing;
  b.  ACCEPT  the determination  that the adoption  of Resolution  No. 2024-02A  is exempt  from  the California
  Envirorunental  Quality  Act ("CEQA"),  codified  at Public  Resources  Code  §§ 21000  et seq.), pursuant  to
  Public Resources Code 8321080.17, and that the adoption of Resolution No. 2024-02B is "categorically
  exempt"  from  CEQA  under  the regulatory  guidelines  established  under  CEQA  ("CEQA  Guidelines"),
  codified  at Cliapter  3 of Division  6 of Title  14 of the California  Code of Regulations  ("CCR"),  as a Class
  6 exemption  (Information  Collection)  under 14 CCR  § 15306  and is also "statutorily  exempt"  from CEQA
  under  the Feasibility  and Planning  Studies  exemption  established  by the CEQA  Guidelines  at 14 CCR
  § 15262;
  c.  DISAPPROVE,  AND  DO NOT  ADOPT,  Resolution  No. 2024-02A,  which  resolution  recommends  the
  immediate  removal  of  size  restrictions  for  warehouses  in  the  City's  Urban  Mixed  Use  Zones  and
  Commercial  Industrial  Zones.
  d.  TAKE  ACTION  ON  Resolution  No.  2024-02B  by either  approving  and adopting  or disapproving  and
  choosing  not to adopt  that resolution.  Staff  has no preference  or recommendation  as to the approval  or

  1

   disapproval  of Resolution  No.  2024-02B,  except that if the Commission  approves  and adopts  Resolution
  No. 2024-02A,  then Staff recommends  disapproving  and not adopting  Resolution  No. 2024-02B.

PUBLIC  NOTIFICATION:  Advertising  and notification  of the public  hearing  for this item  was conducted  in
compliance  with  South  Gate Municipal  Code  Sections  11.50.020  and 11.50.030.  Notice  of the hearing  was
originally  posted  and published  in the "South  Gate Press"  on February  24, 2024.

The original  public  hearing  was scheduled  for March  5, 2024.  Since,  at the request  of the Applicant,  the public
hearing was continued  at the March  5'h meeting to a "date  certain"  (April  16(h), no additional  public  notice  is
required, aside from that described in the above paragraph.

ENVIRONMENTAL  EVALUATION:  Adoption  of Resolution  No.  2024-02A  is exempt  from  CEQA  for two
reasons.  First,  amendment  of a zoning  code ordinance  only  constitutes  a "project"  under  CEQA  if it has the
potential for resulting in direct or indirect physical changesto the environment, per 14 CCR el 15378.  This
proposed  amendment  will  not cause  physical  changes  to the environment,  because  it does not exempt  future
warehouse  projects  from Conditional  Use Permit  and CEQA  compliance  requirements.  The proposed  amendment
is therefore  exempt  from  CEQA  because  it does not meet the definition  of a CEQA  project.  Second,  even if it
were to be deemed a project, it has no potential for causing  a significant  effect  on the environment  and is therefore
exempt from CEQA pursuant to 14 CCR § 15061.

Adoption  of Resolution  No.  2024-02B  is also exempt  from  CEQA  for two  reasons.  First,  it is categorically
exempt  from  CEQA  as a Class 6 exemption  under  14 CCR  § 15306.  Class  6 exempts  activities  consisting  of
"basic  data collection,  research,  experimental  management,  and resource  evaluation  activities  which  do not result
in a serious  or major  disturbance  to an environmental  resource.  These  may be strictly  for information  gathering
purposes,  or as part of a study  leading  to an action  which  a public  agency  has not yet approved,  adopted,  or
funded."  Second,  it is also statutorily  exempt  from  CEQA  as Feasibility  and Planning  Studies  under  the CEQA
Guidelines  at 14 CCR  § 15262.  That  exemption  exempts  projects  "involving  only  feasibility  or planning  studies
for possible  future  actions  which  the agency,  board,  or commission  has not approved,  adopted,  or funded  does
not require  the preparation  of an EIR  or negative  declaration  but does require  consideration  of environmental
factors."

BACKGROUND:  The Zoning  Code,  together  with  the City's  General  Plan,  Specific  Plans  and Zoning  Map,
divides  the City  into various  geographical  use zones.  Land  use permission  tables  in Section  11.21.030  of the
Zoning  Code establish  the uses to which  land in each zone may be put.  Table  11.21-3  specifies  uses allowed  in
theUrbanMixed-Usezones,andTablell.21-4specifiesusesallowedintheCommercialIndustrialzones.  Under
those  tables,  warehousing  is permitted  (subject  to issuance  by the City  of a Conditional  Use  Permit)  in the
Industrial  Flex  (IF),  Light  Industrial  (LF),  Light  Manufacturing  (M2)  and Heavy  Manufacturing  (M3)  zones.
However,  footnote  18 in Table  11.21-3  and Footnote  11 in Table  11.21-4  each limits  the size and placement  of
warehouses  within  those zones as follows:

  "Limited  to maximum  building  area of fi'Jieen  thousand  square  feet and is not permitted  along
  street frontage  (would  have to be a rear use)."

These  footnotes  were  incorporated  into  the South  Gate Municipal  Code  in 2015  when  the Commission  and
Council  cohesively  adopted  a comprehensive  update  to the Zoning  Code.  The Planning  Commissioners  and City
Council  Members  who were in office  at that time  felt the inclusion  of these footnotes  was necessary  to prevent  a

  8
 proliferation  of large warehouses  in the City  which  would  cause detrimental  impacts  to the cornrnunity.

Recently,  landowners  and developers  have expressed  to Staff  (and in some cases to Planning  Commissioners  and
to City  Council  Members)  the landowners'  and developers'  opinions  tliat  tlie  limitations  imposed  by  these
footnotes  are outdated,  are  unduly  restrictive,  and  create  limitations  inconsistent  with  the  current  business
practices  of the warehousing  industry.  They  have asked the City  to consider  eliminating  the footnotes  entirely,
or at least modifying  them to loosen the restrictions  and allow  the construction  and operation  of larger warehouses
in the City.

ANALYSIS:

In response  to those requests,  Staff  is presenting  to the Commission  two  separate  resolutions.  Resolution  No.
2024-02A,  if adopted  by  the  Commission,  would  recommend  to the City  Council  that  the Zoning  Code  be
amended  to delete those footnotes  from  the land use permission  tables.  Resolution  No. 2024-02B,  if adopted  by
the Commission,  would  direct  Staff to evaluate  the effects  of modifying  or entirely  eliminating  the footnotes.

Staff  does not recommend  the adoption  of Resolution  No. 2024-02A.  Deletion  of the subject  footnotes  from  the
Zoning  Code would  eliminate  the 15,000  square foot size restriction  applicable  to warehouses  in the City.  Absent
that restriction,  the only  limitations  on warehouse  size would  be those generally  applicable  to other buildings  in
the respective  zones imposed  by things  such as setback  requirements,  height  limitations,  and floor-area-ratio
requirements.  This will  undoubtedly  lead to the construction  of warehouses  in the City  which  are much  larger
than those currently  found  in the City.  Without  further  study  or other limitations,  Staff  is unable  to predict  - or
advise  the Commission  as to - the effects  such larger  warehouses  might  have on traffic,  infrastructure,  noise and
other matters  important  to residents  of the City.

ResolutionNo.2024-02BispresentedasanalternativetoResolutionNo.2024-02A.  RatherthanResolutionNo.
2024-02A's  "all  or nothing"  approach  of eliminating  or retaining  the current  restrictions  on warehouse  size and
location  restrictions,  Resolution  No. 2024-02B  provides  an opportunity  for Staff to evaluate  whether  and to what
extent  those restrictions  should  be eliminated,  modified  or retained.  Resolution  No. 2024-02B  would  allow  Staff
to return to the Commission  at a later date with  an analysis  of benefits  and detriments  of modifying  or eliminating
those restrictions,  as well  as whether  additional  development  standards  or operating  practices  should  be imposed
in  connection  with  the construction  and operation  of larger  warehouses.  In this way,  the Commission  can make
a more informed  decision.

CONCLUSION:  If the  Commission  believes  the  current  restrictions  on warehouse  size and  location  are
unreasonable  and should  be changed,  Staff  recommends  adopting  Resolution  No.  2024-02B  but not Resolution
No.  2024-02A.  If the Commission  believes  the current  restrictions  are reasonable,  Staff  recommends  that both
resolutions  be disapproved  and neither  be adopted.
